intro.kicker: The way of training taking the world by storm
intro.title: What is hybrid training?
text: Hybrid training combines endurance and strength in the same session: 1 km running legs alternated with functional workout stations. Eight running blocks and eight stations to build an aerobic engine and strength that hold up when your heart rate is high.
It is the perfect preparation for hybrid fitness races and for anyone who wants to be truly fit. Endurance and strength in a single workout. For every level.

stations.name: SkiErg
stations.tip: Use your hips, not just your arms. Sustainable pace: there are still 7 km to go.

stations.name: Sled Push
stations.tip: Arms extended, body low, short and steady steps.

stations.name: Sled Pull
stations.tip: Walk backwards and pull with your whole body, not just your arms.

stations.name: Burpee Broad Jumps
stations.tip: Steady, medium jumps beat maximum jumps with long pauses.

stations.name: Farmers Carry
stations.tip: Shoulders back, quick steps. Putting the weights down costs more than keeping going.

stations.name: Sandbag Lunges
stations.tip: Knee touches the ground on every lunge. Breathe with every step.

stations.name: Wall Balls
stations.tip: Fixed sets from the start (e.g. 10–15) and short rests.

weightsNote: Open division weights for guidance only, as commonly used in hybrid fitness competitions. Always check the rulebook of the event you enter.

divisions.name: Open
divisions.text: The standard division. Ideal for your first hybrid race.

divisions.name: Pro
divisions.text: Same course, heavier loads. For experienced athletes.

divisions.name: Doubles
divisions.text: In pairs: you run together and split the work at the stations.

divisions.name: Relay
divisions.text: Teams of 4: each athlete does 2 km and 2 stations.

whyUs.title: Competition equipment
whyUs.text: Sleds, SkiErg, rowers, wall balls and sandbags to competition standards. You train exactly what you will face on race day.

whyUs.title: A real endurance base
whyUs.text: We come from triathlon and running. We know how to build the aerobic engine that makes the difference over the 8 km of running.

whyUs.title: Strength that doesn't slow you down
whyUs.text: Functional strength programming designed to perform with a high heart rate, not to lift more in a gym.

whyUs.title: Simulations and strategy
whyUs.text: Monthly timed race simulations, station-by-station split analysis and a pacing and nutrition strategy for race day.

faq.q: Do I need previous experience to start?
faq.a: No. We adapt loads and volume to your level. Many of our athletes start without ever having done a sled push.

faq.q: How long do I need to prepare for my first hybrid race?
faq.a: With a general fitness base, 8 to 16 weeks of specific preparation is enough to reach your first Open race with confidence.

faq.q: Can I combine the box with my running or triathlon plan?
faq.a: Yes, and it's one of our specialities. We integrate the box sessions with your endurance plan so they don't clash.

faq.q: Do you organise race registration and travel?
faq.a: We advise you on choosing the race and division, and we organise group trips to competitions when there are enough athletes from the box.
Of course. The first trial session is free. Message us on WhatsApp or through the contact form.
